newsitem.title: USA: Dole preaches trust and tax cuts in Michigan.
newsitem.headline: Dole preaches trust and tax cuts in Michigan.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole took his message of trust and tax cuts to the must-win state of Michigan on Monday, trying to slice President Bill Clinton's commanding lead in the polls.

Kicking off a two-day campaign trip to the state, Dole held an economic forum with a half dozen Republican governors and vice presidential running-mate Jack Kemp that plugged his plan to cut federal income taxes by 15 percent.

Michigan is a swing state that is part of a bloc of Midwestern states analysts say Dole must win to offset Clinton's advantage in the most populous states such as New York and California. Polls show Dole well behind in Michigan.

The crowd in the cavernous Detroit Diesel plant heard governors charge that Clinton was taking credit for an improved economy that they claimed was largely due to tax cuts and economic reforms they had pushed through in their states.
Dole attacked the president for being two-faced.

"President Clinton ... he's a real talker," Dole said, charging that Clinton was taking credit for millions of new jobs he did not create. "He goes right past the facts, the facts never get in the way."

The latest Reuters daily tracking poll released on Monday showed Clinton had regained a double-digit lead over Dole, leading the Republican by 46.6 to 35.8 percent. The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, showed that Dole's upsurge following the second presidential debate last week was brief and Clinton was again stretching his lead.
With only 15 days left until the election, Dole sounded almost wistful, wondering why so few people had watched the second televised debate between him and the president.

"The election is about two weeks from now and a lot of people haven't focused ... maybe there's no interest in politics, maybe nobody cares or they're just getting around to focusing on it," he said, adding that he expected to win.

Dole, who called on Sunday for banning all campaign contributions from non-U.S.citizens, again criticised Democrats for questionable donations from individuals with ties to an Indonesian real estate and banking conglomerate.

One Republican governor absent from the forum was Wisconsin's Tommy Thompson, who has publicly criticised the Dole campaign in recent days, complaining the Kansas Republican should have let the governors take the lead.

"Tommy is very outspoken, that's a Wisconsin trait, I guess," said Michigan Republican Gov. John Engler. He said he expected Dole to win Michigan by about two percentage points despite polls showing the Republican trailing badly here.

Engler voiced a complaint common among governors here, saying "it's the work being done at the state level that has really changed America. ... it has partially offset what Bill Clinton has tried to do to us in Washington."
Dole will travel across the state by bus for the rest of Monday and Tuesday.
